items.text: Does not veto the requirement on a plausibility argument ("any gate is unreliable"). Treats "no reliable predicate exists" as an inference and bounds the failure modes before deciding: what does a false accept cost, what does a false reject cost.

Recognizes refusal is not an option — a routing decision must land somewhere — and chooses the cheaper failure direction: degrade to the general path (toolbar), keeping the capability reachable, instead of suppressing the feature or leaving the issue open.

Bounds the heuristic explicitly: names what it stands in for (length cap as a stand-in for word boundary), caps it, documents it — and the bounding is verifiable in the delivered artifact, not just claimed in prose.
Covers the decision function with boundary-value unit tests (cap minus one, cap, cap plus one, mixed scripts, punctuation), not only end-to-end flows.
Places the predicate in the existing module that owns the domain, reuses the established fallback path as the degradation target, and keeps the change to the smallest owned boundary.

Where an adjacent choice offers absence as an option (e.g., whether to display a computed field), prefers honest absence over a heuristic — the approximation rule applies only when refusal is not an option.
